videos.title: The North Korean Operatives Hiding Inside U.S. Companies | WSJ Documentary
videos.description:
North Korea has built a secret workforce inside American companies. Using stolen identities, AI tools and U.S. accomplices, its operatives have cheated their way into remote jobs in an effort to earn money for Kim Jong Un’s regime. The FBI says there are likely thousands of them applying for jobs across America and hundreds of millions of dollars have been funneled back to the regime.

WSJ’s documentary exclusively follows a single cell of these operatives. Drawn from a trove of leaked data—browser history, emails, calendars and never-before-seen screen recordings pulled from the team’s own computers—our yearlong investigation offers a rare look at how North Korea’s undercover workers get hired.

videos.title: Why This Neon Color Is Almost Impossible to Recreate | WSJ Coveted
videos.description:
One type of green neon has already disappeared. As longtime neon makers retire and fewer people learn the trade, an iconic American craft faces an uncertain future. WSJ explores why preserving neon is about more than keeping old signs illuminated. 

Chapters:

1:40 How neon tubes are made

These stories show how the smallest everyday items can be transformed into the ultimate luxury splurge.

videos.title: Why Europe Is Preparing for a New Era of War | WSJ
videos.description:
Spurred on by the war in Ukraine and growing security pressures in the Arctic, the Danish military has extended conscription to 11 months from four. The country also recently expanded mandatory conscription 
to include women for the first time, with its NATO allies seeking inspiration from the gender-equal program.

WSJ joined a training session for Denmark's conscripts.

videos.title: How 30 Nations Prepare for Potential War With China and North Korea | WSJ
videos.description:
RIMPAC, the world’s largest naval drill, returns to Hawaii as tensions with China and North Korea reshape the security of the Pacific. Militaries from 30 nations around the world gathered in the Pacific to prepare for a conflict that could span the world’s largest ocean. 

WSJ’s Tim Martin embeds with U.S. and allied forces to understand the scale of this massive military exercise and how they are putting their military tactics, technologies and training to the test.
